messages:
Maria (PM): Morning — quick async on the Wavefront rollout (feature flag: wavefront_v2). Currently at 7% traffic slice.

Maria (PM): What I did: kicked off the gradual ramp at 03:40 PT, validated smoke tests, and hooked the new metric tags into dashboard.

Maria (PM): Observations: p95 latency for /generate up ~18ms (baseline 220ms -> now ~238ms), error rate for that route up from 0.3% -> 0.9% (small spike), CPU on a few hosts showing short bursts. No customer-facing incidents.

Maria (PM): Blockers / concerns: we see occasional 502s originating from the blue pool when requests > 2k/min. Not sure if kv-cache eviction or recent kernel patch is implicated.

Maria (PM): Today / ask: want agreement on holding at 7% for another 2h to gather traces + flamegraphs, or do we abort and rollback to wavefront_v1? Also request SRE to enable request-level debug logging for three sample IDs I posted to the dashboard.

Alex (Eng): Saw the same spike locally in staging when I replayed a 10K req/min slice. Logs show `kv_cache_miss` events clustered before the 502s. Could be cache pressure + an unhandled nil in our handler.

Alex (Eng): Quick patch ready (small nil-check + counter) — will open PR if we decide to continue ramp. If rollback chosen I can trigger quick revert.

Jin (Infra): Looking at host metrics: those blue pool machines had a short oom_kill on one instance at 03:42 PT but it recovered. Kernel patch 5.15.0-99 rolled yesterday to that AZ only — suspicious. I'm rolling a canary of the old kernel to one host for comparison.

Sam (SRE): sre-bot summary: alert `backend_502_rate` triggered 3 times in last 30m (avg 0.6% spike). No paged incidents. Linking alert: https://monitoring.internal/alerts/4821 :eyes:

Sam (SRE): I can enable debug logs for the three sample requests Maria mentioned, but that will increase log volume ~4x. Suggest we limit debug window to 30m.

Carla (Product): Not comfortable with further ramp until we rule out kernel/infra as root cause. Customer risk is medium for this route. Recommend hold at 7% and run the extra traces.

Maria (PM): Thanks — noted. My preference is hold + gather traces. If Alex's patch looks like it addresses nil-check quickly we can patch behind the flag and re-evaluate.

Alex (Eng): I can cut the PR now (WIP). If we push the patch behind the FF we should be able to test safely at 7% without user impact.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: branch=fix/kv-nil-check user=alex status=queued (build 8942).

Sam (SRE): I'll enable 30m debug window now and add a tracing span on those hosts. Also creating short-lived dashboard: https://dashboard.internal/queries/wavefront_v2_debug

Carla (Product): Veto ramp for now. Please do not move above 7% until infra confirms kernel not causal.

Alex (Eng): Acknowledged. Pausing any automated ramp steps. PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/wavefront/merge_requests/512 — includes test & rollback plan.

Maria (PM): Decision summary: hold at 7% for 2h, enable 30m debug logs + traces, Jin will roll one node back to previous kernel for comparison, Alex will open PR and be on standby for quick patch deploy behind FF. If debug traces look clean and no kernel correlation we reconvene in ~2h to consider 25% ramp.

Maria (PM): Ping me in this thread with final thumbs when you're ok to proceed. :thumbsup: :eyes:

Alex (Eng): +1 from eng side (ready to patch).

Jin (Infra): Rolling back one host now, will report results in ~15m.

Sam (SRE): Debug window active — will post any hit summaries here.

Carla (Product): Veto remains until infra confirms.

sre-bot: alert clear: backend_502_rate (recent spike suppressed by debug window).

Maria (PM): Thanks all — holding for now. I will post final decision at 1958766010.
